misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.inflections#no_doubling: Watch the doubling rule: after one short vowel and one final consonant, double the consonant before -ing or -ed (run → running, stop → stopped).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.inflections#kept_silent_e: Drop the silent e before an ending that starts with a vowel (make → making, hope → hoping).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.inflections#y_not_changed: After a consonant, y changes to i before -ed, -er, -est or -es (carry → carried, happy → happier).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.inflections#over_doubling: Only double when the last syllable is stressed or the word is short (open → opening, visit → visited).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.homophones#contraction_posses: An apostrophe here means letters are missing (it's = it is, you're = you are). Belonging words have no apostrophe: its, your, whose.
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.homophones#familiar_spelling: These words sound the same, so check the meaning of the sentence before choosing the spelling.
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.homophones#near_homophone: These words sound nearly alike but mean different things: check which meaning the sentence needs.
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.morphological#dropped_double_: Where two parts join with the same letter, keep both letters (mis + spell = misspell, real + ly = really).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.morphological#full_suffix: The suffix -ful has only one l (hopeful, careful).
misconceptions.EN.FND.SPL.morphological#suffix_by_sound: -able and -ible (and -tion and -sion) sound alike, so the sound cannot decide. -able usually follows a whole word (readable).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.VERB.present_past_simple#regulari: This verb is irregular: it does not take -ed in the past (go → went, buy → bought).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.VERB.present_past_simple#past_aft: After did or didn't, use the base form of the verb (Did you go? not Did you went?).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.VERB.present_past_simple#tense_sh: Keep the same time through the sentence: if it starts in the past, stay in the past.
misconceptions.EN.GRM.VERB.sva#third_person_s: With he, she, it or one person or thing, the present-tense verb takes -s (she goes, it rains).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.VERB.sva#attraction_error: Match the verb to the real subject, not to the noun just before the verb (The box of pencils is…).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.articles#article_omission: A singular countable noun needs a, an or the (She is a teacher).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.articles#article_with_uncoun: Uncountable nouns such as advice and information do not take a or an (some advice).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.articles#a_an_sound: Choose a or an by the first sound, not the first letter (an hour, a university).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.plurals_countability#plural_: Uncountable nouns have no plural: information, advice, furniture (not informations).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.plurals_countability#regular: This plural is irregular (child → children, mouse → mice).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.NOUN.plurals_countability#much_ma: Use many with things you can count and much with things you cannot (many books, much water).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.PUN.capitalisation#lowercase_prop: Names of particular people, places, days and months start with a capital letter (Chennai, Monday).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.PUN.capitalisation#random_capital: Ordinary nouns do not take capitals, even important ones (my school, the river).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.PUN.apostrophes#plural_apostrophe: A plain plural has no apostrophe (mangoes for sale).
misconceptions.EN.GRM.PUN.apostrophes#its_with_apostrop: its (belonging to it) has no apostrophe; it's always means it is or it has.
misconceptions.EN.GRM.PUN.apostrophes#possessive_positi: For several owners ending in s, the apostrophe goes after the s (the girls' bags).
misconceptions.EN.VOC.BRD.general#sound_alike_confusion: This word looks or sounds like another one: check the meaning in the sentence.
misconceptions.EN.VOC.MOR.prefixes#wrong_negative_prefi: The negative prefix depends on the base word: im- before b, m, p; il- before l; ir- before r (impossible, illegal, irregular).
misconceptions.EN.VOC.MOR.prefixes#prefix_meaning_confu: These prefixes look alike but mean different things (pre- before, pro- for; inter- between, intra- within).
misconceptions.EN.VOC.MOR.suffixes#wrong_word_class: Right word family, wrong kind of word: describing a verb needs the -ly adverb (spoke confidently).
misconceptions.EN.VOC.MOR.suffixes#invented_derivation: That form does not exist; this word family uses a different ending (happiness, decision).
misconceptions.EN.VOC.REL.synonyms_antonyms#related_not: That word is from the same topic, but it does not mean the same thing.
misconceptions.EN.VOC.REL.synonyms_antonyms#synonym_ant: Check the question: does it ask for a word with the same meaning or the opposite meaning?
